newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: SQUASH-JANSHER KHAN BRUSHES ASIDE ENGLAND'S PARKE.
newsitem.headline: SQUASH-JANSHER KHAN BRUSHES ASIDE ENGLAND'S PARKE.

text.p: Pakistan's Jansher Khan moved a step closer to a record eighth World Open title on Wednesday when he brushed aside England's Simon Parke 15-3 15-4 15-8.
Jansher, the 27-year-old top seed, will now meet third seed Peter Nicol of Scotland, who defeated Australia's Craig Rowland in straight games in an earlier quarter-final.
Australia's Rodney Eyles, the second seed, was pushed to the limit by Zubair Jahan of Pakistan, who looked set to create a major upset when he led 2-0 in games and 12-10 in the third.
In a tense match, Eyles received a conduct warning from Singapore referee Desmond Hill for barging in the second game.

The Australian complained when his opponent fell after they collided, arguing that Zubair had received lets for the merest contact and that he was unable to pursue the ball without the Pakistani falling over.
"I thought I was gone when he got ahead again in third game," Eyles said.

A brace of penalty strokes to the Australian in the backhand court brought him to 13-13 and a splendid forehand overhead smash set up his first of three game balls. Eyles then dominated the match to advance to the semifinals.

"I have played Zubair before. It is all emotion with him," Eyles said. "Some matches are more of a fight than a squash game. You just have to survive long enough to finish them off. I am looking forward to the semifinal tomorrow when we can get back to playing squash."
Eyles will now meet England's Chris Walker, the fifth seed, who upset third seeded Australian Brett Martin in four games.
